title: Pennsylvania doctor urges vaccination as measles outbreak grows - PBS

analysis.time: The CDC has confirmed more than 4,000 cases of measles this year as the country grapples with the largest outbreak of the highly infectious virus in 35 years. Pennsylvania is the epicenter of the outbreak with more than 1,100 cases. That includes five measles-related deaths and potentially a sixth still being investigated.
analysis.location_and_population: Nearly a fifth of cases comprise children under the age of five, and 95% are among unvaccinated people.
analysis.event: A Pennsylvania doctor, Dr. Evan Shirey, discusses the measles outbreak and its severe impact on young children, emphasizing the consequences of the virus and the role of vaccine hesitancy. The CDC has confirmed more than 4,000 cases of measles this year, marking the largest outbreak in 35 years. [N10, N18, N21, N24, N25, N26, N27].
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The CDC has confirmed more than 4,000 cases of measles this year, with Pennsylvania being the epicenter. There are five measles-related deaths and potentially a sixth still under investigation. The outbreak has led to severe complications, including encephalitis and bronchopneumonia, requiring hospitalization and in some cases, ventilator support. [N10, N18, N19, N26, N27, N31, N38, N39, N40].
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC has confirmed the measles outbreak, and the situation is being actively addressed by healthcare professionals. The outbreak is attributed to vaccine hesitancy, and Dr. Shirey urges vaccination to prevent further spread. The exact cause of the outbreak and the potential sixth death are still under investigation. [N10, N18, N19, N21, N24, N25, N26, N27, N50, N52].

analysis.brief_en: A measles outbreak in the United States has reached its largest scale in 35 years, with the CDC confirming over 4,000 cases this year. Pennsylvania is the epicenter, reporting more than 1,100 cases, including five deaths and a potential sixth under investigation. The outbreak has disproportionately affected unvaccinated individuals, particularly children under five. Dr. Evan Shirey, a pediatric infectious disease doctor in Hershey, Pennsylvania, highlights the severe health consequences, such as encephalitis and bronchopneumonia, which have led to hospitalizations and, in some cases, the need for ventilator support. The outbreak is attributed to declining vaccination rates, and Shirey emphasizes the importance of vaccination to prevent further spread. The situation is being actively managed by healthcare professionals, but the exact cause of the outbreak and the status of the potential sixth death remain under investigation. The outbreak underscores the risks associated with vaccine hesitancy and the resurgence of a virus that was previously eliminated in the country.

Dr. Evan Shirey, a pediatric infectious disease doctor in Hershey, Pennsylvania, highlights the severe health consequences, such as encephalitis and bronchopneumonia, which have led to hospitalizations and, in some cases, the need for ventilator support. The outbreak is attributed to declining vaccination rates, and Shirey emphasizes the importance of vaccination to prevent further spread. The situation is being actively managed by healthcare professionals, but the exact cause of the outbreak and the status of the potential sixth death remain under investigation. The outbreak underscores the risks associated with vaccine hesitancy and the resurgence of a virus that was previously eliminated in the country.
